title: Client protocol negotiation, prefetch controls, and graceful shutdown requirements for SDKs
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Background: As Redwood expands SDK support across Python, TypeScript, and Go we have uncovered subtle interoperability and user-experience gaps around streaming shutdowns, client-driven prefetching, and protocol version negotiation. Product teams need a clear multi-language contract that prevents data loss, avoids unexpected duplicate events during retries, and preserves zero-downtime upgrades for hosted and dedicated deployments.

This ticket is a PRD that defines the requirements and acceptance criteria for (1) a small, explicit protocol negotiation header and runtime handshake so SDKs can opt into new behaviors; (2) a client-side prefetch and backpressure control surface for paginated and streaming endpoints; and (3) a graceful shutdown/drain mechanism exposed uniformly across Python/TS/Go SDKs. The goal is to enable safe rollouts of runtime-side changes without breaking long-lived streaming consumers or paginated cursor semantics.
scope: Define a protocol negotiation header and semantics (minor versioning and capability flags).
Standardize cursor semantics for paginated reads across SDKs including: opaque cursor format, expiry, and resumability guarantees.
Specify a prefetch/backpressure surface that allows clients to control lookahead, max-inflight, and memory budgets for paging and streaming APIs.
Design a graceful shutdown API for client runtimes: synchronous drain, configurable deadlines, and optional force-close.
Provide a compatibility test matrix and a reference implementation for Python; TS and Go SDKs will implement parity behaviors.
Define telemetry and observable signals (metrics/logs/traces) that must be emitted for rollouts, retries, and shutdowns.
out_of_scope: Server-side runtime kernel scheduling changes (handled in runtime roadmap).
Large-scale refactors of existing pagination endpoints — this ticket only defines client-side contract and shims.
New UI/Console features for debugging SDK drains (separate observability work).
requirements: R1: Protocol negotiation header 'X-RI-SDK-Capabilities' with a JSON-safe client fingerprint string and semantic version field. Server should respond with 'X-RI-Server-Mode' to indicate compatibility behavior.
R2: Pagination cursor contract: cursors are opaque strings; server guarantees monotonic forward progress and best-effort resume for up to 7 days. SDKs must expose 'cursor_expires_at' when provided.
R3: Prefetch controls: SDK constructors expose 'prefetch_pages', 'max_inflight_requests', and an optional 'memory_budget_bytes' hint. Default values conservative for browser/edge environments.

R4: Streaming API backpressure: streaming client must allow callers to pause/resume consumption and specify per-stream 'ack' window size. Implementations must avoid unbounded memory growth when prefetch/backpressure limits are hit.

R5: Graceful shutdown: SDKs expose 'shutdown(ctx, drain_timeout_ms)' (or idiomatic equivalent) which triggers: stop accepting new requests, wait for inflight requests up to deadline, flush buffered prefetch queues, and optionally return a detailed shutdown report (counts: drained, timed_out, forced_closed).

R6: Retries and idempotency: SDKs must implement idempotent retry semantics for non-streaming endpoints using idempotency tokens where available, and clearly document which streaming/paginated operations are not safe to retry transparently.
R7: Compatibility guarantees: new server-capability flags must only enable additive behaviors; any breaking change requires an explicit Major protocol bump and a migration guide.

R8: Telemetry hooks: SDKs emit metrics for 'prefetch_bytes', 'inflight_count', 'drain_duration_ms', 'protocol_mismatch', and a compatibility 'fingerprint' tag on traces. Metrics must be taggable by customer and route.

R9: Tests: each SDK must include unit tests for cursor resume, integration tests against a compatibility shim, and a chaos test that simulates mid-stream server restart and ensures drain semantics hold.
api_surface: Client(config) - config includes: prefetch_pages, max_inflight_requests, memory_budget_bytes, enable_protocol_negotiation
list_resources(parent, page_size, cursor=None) -> PaginatedIterator with .next() and .resume(cursor)
RetryPolicy(policy_name) helper and high-level wrappers that enforce idempotency tokens for safe retry paths
migration_plan: Phase 1 (alpha): Publish protocol negotiation header and reference Python implementation behind feature flag. Add unit/integration tests in CI.
Phase 2 (beta): Release Python SDK with default conservative prefetch values and opt-in negotiation for TS/Go contributors. Run compatibility test sweep across major customers.
Phase 3 (GA): Enable negotiation by default; publish migration guide and remove temporary shims. Coordinate server-side rollout with runtime team to honor 'X-RI-SDK-Capabilities' flags.
Rollback: Server will honor a 'compat_mode' header that forces legacy behavior if client negotiation indicates a mismatch.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Protocol negotiation header roundtrip validated in integration tests; server echoes capability decisions and clients respect server direction.
AC2: SDKs expose prefetch/backpressure controls in public API and documentation; default values set for browser and server contexts and validated in perf tests.
AC3: Graceful shutdown API drains inflight requests and prefetch queues within configured deadline in 90% of runs under normal load; a clear error/report produced on timeout.

AC4: Cursor resume behavior validated: after simulated transient error and resume with cursor, iterator continues without duplication for >95% of test records (tolerate edge-case duplicates documented).
AC5: Streaming pause/resume preserves message ordering and does not leak memory when paused for long durations in unit/CI memory tests.
AC6: Compatibility test matrix completed: every supported SDK version passes compatibility shim tests for minor server behavior flags; documented exceptions listed in migration guide.
AC7: Telemetry metrics emitted and visible in the staging observability stack for prefetch, inflight, drain duration, and protocol mismatch events.
performance_targets: PT1: Default prefetch must not increase median memory usage of the SDK host process by more than 8% for typical paging workloads.
PT2: Drain operation for 100 concurrent inflight requests should complete within 5 seconds 90th percentile under normal load when drain_timeout_ms is 10_000.
PT3: Pagination roundtrip latency should not increase by more than 5% when protocol negotiation is enabled.
observability_and_testing: Add CI integration job 'sdk-compatibility-sweep' that runs the compatibility shim matrix across Python/TS/Go nightly.
Add unit tests that validate Cursor serialization/deserialization and expiry semantics.
Add chaos test that kills the server mid-stream and asserts client drain semantics and no silent data loss.
Expose debug logs for shutdown flow behind 'RI_SDK_DEBUG=1' environment flag.
